med-sci.title: Admission requirements for every Canadian medical school (AFMC)
med-sci.what: A free yearly guide to all 19 Canadian medical schools: MCAT rules, seats, dates, fees and contacts. Use it to compare schools before you apply.

med-sci.title: Apply to Ontario medical schools through OMSAS
med-sci.what: Step-by-step: how an application to Ontario medical schools goes through OMSAS, including transcripts, releasing MCAT scores and checking your file is complete.

med-sci.title: Take the MCAT with accommodations (AAMC)
med-sci.what: How to ask for extra time, breaks or other changes on the MCAT if you have a disability or health condition, and how to book once approved.

med-sci.title: Ask for Casper accommodations (Acuity Insights)
med-sci.what: How to request accommodations for the Casper test: the form, supporting documents, where to send them and the deadline.

med-sci.title: What medical school costs: U of T MD tuition 2026-27
med-sci.what: One school's official fee table for first-year medicine, plus its estimate for books and living costs. A real example to start a budget from.

med-sci.title: Paid summer research for undergrads (NSERC USRA)
med-sci.what: A paid, full-time summer research job in a university lab, for undergraduate science and engineering students. Good first research experience.

med-sci.title: Canadian Association of Physicians with Disabilities: pre-med resources
med-sci.what: A Canadian network of doctors and medical learners with disabilities. This page lists programs that help disabled students apply to medical school.

public-health.title: Nursing routes in Ontario: RN degree or RPN diploma (College of Nurses of Ontario)
public-health.what: Explains which school programs lead to each kind of nursing licence in Ontario, with lists of approved university and college programs.

public-health.title: Accommodations on nursing registration exams (College of Nurses of Ontario)
public-health.what: How to ask for changes to exam conditions on the nursing registration exams if a disability or health condition affects how you write tests.

public-health.title: Free pre-med mentoring for disabled students (U of T Community of Support)
public-health.what: A free program with advising, mentors, and help with MCAT, CASPer, applications and interviews for under-represented students, including disabled students.

public-health.title: MCAT Fee Assistance Program for Canadians (AFMC)
public-health.what: Lower MCAT fees and free official prep material for Canadians who could not afford the test otherwise. Check eligibility online, then apply.

public-health.title: Ontario Learn and Stay Grant (nursing, paramedic, lab and family medicine)
public-health.what: Ontario pays tuition and books for some health programs if you agree to work in an underserved region after you graduate.

public-health.title: Become a public health inspector (CIPHI certification)
public-health.what: The steps to become a Certified Public Health Inspector: an accredited degree, a 12-week supervised field practicum, then the certification exams.

education.title: How to apply to college or university in Ontario
education.what: The Ontario government's plain overview: where to apply (ontariocolleges.ca for college, OUAC for university), admission rules, and paying for school.

education.title: Apply to Ontario colleges (ontariocolleges.ca)
education.what: The official application for all Ontario public colleges: make one account, pick your programs, pay the fee, then watch for offers.

education.title: Accommodations after high school: what changes (Transition Resource Guide)
education.what: Explains how getting accommodations at college or university differs from an IEP in high school, and the steps to register with the accessibility office.

education.title: Your right to accommodation at school (Ontario Human Rights Commission)
education.what: The official policy on what schools, colleges and universities must do to accommodate students with disabilities. Useful if a request is refused.

education.title: OSAP for students with disabilities
education.what: How Ontario student aid works if you have a disability: full-time funding at a lighter course load, plus grants for disability-related services and equipment.

education.title: Plan your courses and timetable (example: Western University)
education.what: One university's clear guide for new students: choosing courses, building a timetable without clashes, and when you can register.

education.title: National Educational Association of Disabled Students (NEADS)
education.what: A national charity run by and for disabled post-secondary students, with a scholarships portal, campus disability services lists and job resources.

career.title: Job Bank: jobs and supports for people with disabilities
career.what: The federal job board's page for disabled job seekers: search jobs from employers who say they support people with disabilities, and find employment programs.

career.title: Free help with resumes, interviews and job search (Employment Ontario)
career.what: Ontario's free employment services: help with your resume, interview practice, finding a job, and programs for youth and students.

career.title: Workplace accommodation: your rights and the steps (Canadian Human Rights Commission)
career.what: A step-by-step guide to asking for and setting up workplace accommodations, including what an employer can and can't ask you.

career.title: Disclosure and accommodations at work (Transition Resource Guide)
career.what: Plain-language help with deciding whether and how to tell an employer about a disability, your rights in Ontario, and how to ask for accommodations.

career.title: Specialisterne Canada: jobs for autistic and neurodivergent people
career.what: A Canadian charity that matches autistic and neurodivergent job seekers with employers who want to hire them. Join their talent pool with a form.

career.title: Ready, Willing and Able (autism and intellectual disability employment)
career.what: A national program that helps employers hire people with intellectual disabilities or autism. Job seekers connect through its local employment agency partners.

living.title: Ontario Disability Support Program (ODSP)
living.what: Ontario's monthly income support for adults with disabilities who need help with basic needs and rent: who qualifies, how much, and how to apply online.

living.title: Renting in Ontario: your rights
living.what: What a landlord can and can't do in Ontario: rent increase limits, evictions, ending a lease, when a landlord can enter, and where to get help with disputes.

living.title: Budget Planner (Financial Consumer Agency of Canada)
living.what: A free government tool that builds a monthly budget from your income and expenses. You can save and finish later.

living.title: 211: find local help with housing, food and bills
living.what: Call, text or chat 2-1-1 to find community services near you, like housing help, food banks and benefits, in many languages.

living.title: Life skills checklist for living on your own (Transition Resource Guide)
living.what: A checklist to rate everyday skills like routines, cooking, laundry and money, then ideas for building the ones you want to work on.

adulting.title: Budget Planner (Financial Consumer Agency of Canada)
adulting.what: A free government tool that lays out your income, bills and subscriptions in one monthly budget. You can save and finish later.

adulting.title: Cancelling contracts, gyms and other deals (Ontario consumer rights)
adulting.what: When you can cancel a contract without paying a penalty, how to do it in writing, and how fast a business must refund you.

adulting.title: Free help with phone, internet and TV bill problems (CCTS)
adulting.what: If your phone, internet or TV company won't fix a billing or contract problem, this independent body handles your complaint for free.

adulting.title: Renew your health card or licence, or book a ServiceOntario visit
adulting.what: Do ID tasks online, like renewing a health card or driver's licence, or book an appointment so you don't have to wait in line.

adulting.title: 211 Ontario: one number for community and social services
adulting.what: Call, text or chat 2-1-1 when you don't know who to ask: help with bills, food, housing, benefits and more, near you.

health.title: Find a family doctor or nurse practitioner (Health Care Connect)
health.what: Sign up once and Ontario looks for a family doctor or nurse practitioner near you who is taking new patients.

health.title: Health811: free health advice, any time
health.what: Call 811 or go online for free health advice at any hour, or to find health services near you.

health.title: 9-8-8: Suicide Crisis Helpline
health.what: Call or text 9-8-8 any time if you are thinking about suicide or worried about someone. This page also has ways to feel safer right now.

health.title: Four questions to ask at a medical appointment (Choosing Wisely Canada)
health.what: Four short questions to bring to any appointment so you understand a test or treatment and its options before you agree to it.

health.title: Healthcare toolkit for autistic adults (AASPIRE)
health.what: Worksheets and tips for doctor visits, plus a tool that makes a one-page accommodations report to give your doctor.

relationships.title: Autism Ontario events and meetups
relationships.what: A calendar of local events across Ontario: support groups, meetups, recreation and workshops. Filter by region and look for adult (18+) events.

relationships.title: Autism Ontario adult supports: help finding social opportunities
relationships.what: Autism Ontario's adult team answers questions and gives referrals, including for relationships and social opportunities near you.

relationships.title: Empowering Connections: Autism Canada's national support line
relationships.what: A Canada-wide line where autistic and neurodivergent people can talk with autistic-led staff by phone, chat, Zoom or email.

relationships.title: Making friends: a guide for autistic adults (National Autistic Society)
relationships.what: Practical ideas for meeting people and keeping friendships going, written for autistic adults: small steps, interest-based groups, and managing social anxiety.

relationships.title: PEERS for Young Adults: friendship and dating skills group (Kerry's Place)
relationships.what: A 16-week group where autistic adults learn and practise the social skills for making and keeping friends and dating, with a family member as social coach.

travel.title: Toronto Pearson: sunflower lanyards and practice walk-throughs
travel.what: Toronto Pearson airport's accessibility services: a free sunflower lanyard for hidden disabilities, a practice visit before your trip, and help on the day.

travel.title: Airport security screening with a disability (CATSA)
travel.what: What to expect at airport security if you have a disability or medical need, including the Family and Accessible Line and staying with your companion.

travel.title: GO Transit accessibility: sunflower pins and step-by-step travel guides
travel.what: GO Transit's help for riders with disabilities, including a sunflower pin for hidden disabilities and free visual step-by-step guides for PRESTO, tickets and trip planning.

travel.title: Access 2 Card: for people who need a support person at venues
travel.what: A card from Easter Seals Canada for people who need a support person at movies, attractions and other venues. Check if you qualify, then apply.

nutrition.title: 10 tips for planning meals on a budget (Unlock Food)
nutrition.what: Simple steps for planning a few days of meals, writing a grocery list and using leftovers, so eating well costs less and takes fewer decisions.

nutrition.title: Eating support made by and for autistic and ADHD people (NEDIC NeuroAffirmED)
nutrition.what: Tip sheets and tools about eating difficulties that are common for autistic and ADHD people, and how to get care that fits how your brain works.

nutrition.title: When picky eating is more than picky: ARFID (NEDIC)
nutrition.what: Explains avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder: very limited eating linked to things like textures, colours or a past bad experience with food, its warning signs, and a short self-screen.

nutrition.title: How to find a dietitian, including free ones (Unlock Food)
nutrition.what: Where to find a registered dietitian: free options through health teams and public health units, and paid ones you can search by postal code.

nutrition.title: Free dietitian advice by phone in BC (HealthLink BC 8-1-1)
nutrition.what: In British Columbia, call 8-1-1 for free health advice, including questions for a registered dietitian.

veganism.title: What you need to know about eating vegan (Unlock Food)
veganism.what: A dietitian-written basics page: which nutrients need planning on a vegan diet (like B12, iron, calcium and vitamin D) and which foods supply them.

veganism.title: Cooking with beans, peas and lentils (Unlock Food)
veganism.what: How to buy, choose and cook beans, peas and lentils (canned or dried), a cheap staple for easy plant-based meals.

veganism.title: All about tofu (Unlock Food)
veganism.what: What tofu is, which type to buy for which dish (silken to extra-firm), and simple ways to cook it.

veganism.title: VegTO: Toronto's plant-based community
veganism.what: A Toronto charity with events, resources and volunteering for people who are plant-curious or fully plant-based.

recovery.title: ConnexOntario: find addiction, mental health and gambling services
recovery.what: Call, text, chat or email to find addiction, mental health or problem gambling programs near you in Ontario. They do the searching for you.

recovery.title: Addiction: signs, treatment and self-referral (CAMH)
recovery.what: A large Toronto mental health and addiction hospital explains what addiction is, how treatment works, and how to get help, including referring yourself.

recovery.title: SMART Recovery: free peer support meetings
recovery.what: Free recovery groups, online or in person, led by trained facilitators. No religious content, no long-term commitment, and groups for family and friends too.

recovery.title: BounceBack Ontario: free coaching for low mood, stress and worry
recovery.what: A free program from the Canadian Mental Health Association: phone coaching and online videos to build skills for anxiety, low mood and stress.

recovery.title: 9-8-8: call or text if you're not sure you need help
recovery.what: The national suicide crisis line, for any time things feel too hard. This page helps you decide when to reach out and what to do right away.

creative.title: Canada Council for the Arts: Explore and Create grants
creative.what: Federal arts grants for Canadian artists and groups to research, create, produce and share new work, or for professional development.

creative.title: Paid help to apply for Canada Council grants (Application Assistance)
creative.what: If you are Deaf, disabled or living with mental illness, the Canada Council can pay someone to help you set up an account and write your application.

creative.title: Ontario Arts Council: Deaf and Disability Arts Projects
creative.what: Ontario grants of up to $10,000 for Deaf and disabled artists to create work, produce it, or build their skills through training or mentorship.

creative.title: Tangled Art + Disability (gallery and artist community)
creative.what: A Toronto gallery and organisation for disabled artists: exhibitions, calls for proposals and grants, and a community of disability-identified artists.

creative.title: Workman Arts: arts community for people with mental health and addiction experience
creative.what: A Toronto arts organisation where artists living with mental health or addiction issues take peer-led classes, share work and become members.

entrepreneurship.title: Futurpreneur Startup Program: loans and mentoring for ages 18 to 39
entrepreneurship.what: A Canada-wide program for young founders: a startup loan plus a hand-matched mentor for up to two years, and business planning tools.

entrepreneurship.title: Futurpreneur Side Hustle Program: start small and keep your job
entrepreneurship.what: Financing and mentoring to start or grow a side business while you keep working full time. A lower-pressure way to test an idea.

entrepreneurship.title: Starter Company Plus: training, a mentor and up to $5,000 (Ontario)
entrepreneurship.what: Ontario's program for people starting, expanding or buying a small business: training, one-on-one advice from a local centre, a mentor, and a possible grant.

entrepreneurship.title: Entrepreneurs with Disabilities Program (Community Futures, BC)
entrepreneurship.what: Business planning help, training, coaching and loans for entrepreneurs who have a disability or an ongoing health condition.
